Scenario: 1. Police approaches citizen (no arrest, no stop power invoked)
Red_Book_Topic: 1. When the police stops you; 2. When the police questions you
Law: Federal Constitution; Police Act 1967; Criminal Procedure Code
Exact_Citation: FC Art 5(1): 'No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty save in accordance with law.' PA s.20(3): duties of police officers.
Source_Document: Federal Constitution (Reprint as at 30 Nov 2025) | Police Act 1967 Act 344 (as at 10 May 2024) | Criminal Procedure Code Act 593 (as at 1 Oct 2022) | Malaysian Bar Red Book: The Police and Your Basic Rights (May 2023)
Police_Power: General duty to prevent and detect crime and keep order (PA s.20(3)); may speak to any person. No general statutory power to detain a person merely to question them absent arrest, a licence/vehicle stop under PA s.24, a search under CPC s.17, or a s.111 written order.
Required_Legal_Trigger: None required for a consensual conversation. Detention requires a specific power: arrest (CPC s.23), licence stop (PA s.24(1)(a)), roadblock (PA s.26), search of place (CPC s.17), or investigation order (CPC s.111).
Threshold_Type: None (consensual) / Reasonable suspicion or reasonable grounds once any detention power is invoked
Acceptable_Reasons: Community policing; asking whether a person needs help; seeking witnesses after an incident; following up a report
Examples_Of_Legitimate_Reasons: Incident reported nearby and officer canvassing witnesses | Person matches a description in an active report | Officer offering assistance
Examples_Of_Insufficient_Reasons: No reason given and refusal to say whether the person is under arrest | 'Routine check' with compulsion but no licence/vehicle/search power invoked | Harassment, curiosity, race or appearance alone (FC Art 8(1) equality)
Police_Boundaries: May approach and speak | May request identification | Must not confine or restrain unless a statutory power applies (CPC s.15 defines arrest as touching/confining or submission)
Police_May_Not_Do: Confine a person without arrest or other lawful power (Penal Code ss.339-342 wrongful restraint/confinement) | Use force absent arrest/resistance (CPC s.15(2) only on resisting arrest) | Threaten to arrest a witness to obtain a statement (Red Book 2.4; CPC s.111 is an order to attend, not arrest)
Citizen_Questions: Am I under arrest? | Am I free to leave? | What is the reason for this stop? | May I see your authority card? (plain-clothes) | What is your name and service number?
Verification_Steps: Ask officer's name, rank and service number; note them | Plain-clothes: ask for authority card (certificate of appointment, Police Act s.14); Red Book 1.1-1.2: red card = suspended officer, no authority | Uniformed: read name tag and number (Red Book 1.3); note vehicle plate (Red Book 1.4)
How_To_Verify_Legality: If answer to 'Am I under arrest?' is no and no other stop power is cited, the interaction is consensual and the person may walk away (Red Book 2.3). If 'yes', ask for grounds (FC Art 5(3), CPC s.28A(1)).
Required_Documents: None for a consensual approach. Authority card on request if plain-clothes (PA s.14).
Need_Reasonable_Suspicion: No (consensual); Yes if any detention power invoked
Valid_Warrant_Requirements: Not applicable - no warrant involved in this scenario
Indicators_Of_Invalid_Warrant: Not applicable - no warrant involved in this scenario
Can_Refuse: Yes - may decline to answer questions beyond identity (Red Book 2.1; no statutory duty to answer outside CPC s.112 examination or s.111 order)
Can_Leave: Yes unless told you are under arrest or a specific stop/search/detention power is stated (Red Book 2.3)
Evidence_To_Preserve: Officer name, rank, service number, authority card colour | Date, time, exact location; patrol vehicle plate | Names and contact details of witnesses | Written contemporaneous notes (Red Book 3.3 'Personal Notes') | Any photos/video lawfully taken by bystanders; medical report if injured | Copies of any document handed over (order, warrant, seizure list, receipt)
Red_Flags: Officer refuses to identify | Will not say whether you are under arrest but blocks you from leaving | Demands you follow them to the station without arrest | Asks for money
Foreigner_Notes: Federal Constitution Art 5(3)-(4) rights (grounds, counsel, 24-hour production) apply to 'a person', not only citizens | Art 5(4) proviso: a non-citizen arrested or detained under immigration law must be produced within 14 days, not 24 hours | Art 5(5): clauses (3) and (4) do not apply to an enemy alien | Consular notification (Vienna Convention on Consular Relations Art 36) is not found in any statute reviewed - Requires Independent Verification | Carry passport/visa or a copy; Immigration Act 1959/63 not reviewed - Requires Independent Verification
Escalation_Path: Lodge a police report at any station (CPC s.107) describing the conduct and officer identity | Complain in writing to the Officer in Charge of Police District (OCPD) / State Police Contingent HQ | Complain to Independent Police Conduct Commission (IPCC) - IPCC Act 2022 not among statutes reviewed; Requires Independent Verification | Contact Bar Council Legal Aid Centre (Red Book front page lists LAC numbers) | SUHAKAM complaint (Human Rights Commission of Malaysia Act 1999 not reviewed; Requires Independent Verification) | Unlawful detention: habeas corpus application to High Court, Federal Constitution Art 5(2) | Civil action for wrongful arrest / false imprisonment / trespass; criminal complaint under Penal Code ss.330, 341-342, 348 where applicable
Research_Notes: Statute confers no stand-alone 'stop and question' power on police; detention is lawful only under a specific power. Red Book 2.3 test ('yes' / not allowed to leave / handcuffed = arrest) is guidance consistent with CPC s.15(1).

Scenario: 2. Police asks questions (informal questioning without arrest)
Red_Book_Topic: 2. When the police questions you; 3. Questioning by the police without arrest
Exact_Citation: CPC s.112(2): 'Such person shall be bound to answer all questions relating to the case put to him by that officer: Provided that such person may refuse to answer any question the answer to which would have a tendency to expose him to a criminal charge or penalty or forfeiture.' s.112(4): officer shall first inform the person of subsections (2) and (3).
Source_Document: Criminal Procedure Code Act 593 (as at 1 Oct 2022) | Malaysian Bar Red Book: The Police and Your Basic Rights (May 2023)
Police_Power: Officer making a police investigation may orally examine any person supposed to be acquainted with the facts and must reduce the statement to writing (s.112(1)); may order attendance in writing (s.111(1)).
Required_Legal_Trigger: An ongoing police investigation into an offence (Chapter XIII) in which the person appears to be acquainted with the facts.
Threshold_Type: Investigation in progress (information received under s.107 / s.108)
Acceptable_Reasons: Person witnessed an incident | Person's name arises from a report | Person is the complainant or victim
Examples_Of_Legitimate_Reasons: Taking a witness account after an accident | Clarifying ownership of property found | Following up a lodged report
Examples_Of_Insufficient_Reasons: Questioning with no identified investigation | Fishing for admissions while refusing to say whether the person is a suspect | Threatening arrest for not answering informal questions
Police_Boundaries: Must inform the person of s.112(2)-(3) before examining (s.112(4)) | Statement must be read back and corrections allowed before signing (s.112(5)) | Must not discourage a voluntary statement (s.114)
Police_May_Not_Do: Compel answers that would self-incriminate (s.112(2) proviso) | Use threat, inducement or promise to obtain a statement (Evidence Act s.24; Penal Code s.330) | Arrest solely to obtain a witness statement (Red Book 2.4; s.111 route is written order then Magistrate's warrant s.111(2))
Citizen_Questions: Am I under arrest? | Is this a section 112 examination? Which case/report number? | Am I a witness or a suspect? | May I have a lawyer present? (Red Book 3.3 advises; statute silent for witnesses) | May I read the statement and correct it before signing? (s.112(5))
Verification_Steps: Ask officer's name, rank and service number; note them | Plain-clothes: ask for authority card (certificate of appointment, Police Act s.14); Red Book 1.1-1.2: red card = suspended officer, no authority | Uniformed: read name tag and number (Red Book 1.3); note vehicle plate (Red Book 1.4) | Ask for the report number and investigating officer's name | Ask whether a written s.111 order exists; if informal, you may propose a convenient time/place (Red Book 3.2)
How_To_Verify_Legality: Lawful s.112 examination is tied to an identified investigation; officer must give the s.112(4) caution about duty to answer and right against self-incrimination. Absent an investigation there is no duty to answer.
Required_Documents: Written order under s.111(1) if attendance is being compelled; none for a voluntary interview
Need_Judicial_Approval: No (Magistrate's warrant only if person refuses a s.111 order, s.111(2))
Valid_Warrant_Requirements: Not applicable - no warrant involved in this scenario
Indicators_Of_Invalid_Warrant: Not applicable - no warrant involved in this scenario
Can_Refuse: Partly - must answer questions relating to the case in a s.112 examination except self-incriminating ones (s.112(2)); may refuse to answer anything outside a s.112 examination
Can_Leave: Yes if not arrested and no s.111 order compels attendance now; Red Book 3.2 suggests offering a convenient time
Evidence_To_Preserve: Officer name, rank, service number, authority card colour | Date, time, exact location; patrol vehicle plate | Names and contact details of witnesses | Written contemporaneous notes (Red Book 3.3 'Personal Notes') | Any photos/video lawfully taken by bystanders; medical report if injured | Copies of any document handed over (order, warrant, seizure list, receipt) | Keep your own written record of every question and answer (Red Book 3.3) | Copy of the signed statement if provided
Red_Flags: No caution under s.112(4) | Refusal to let you read or correct the statement | Pressure to sign blank or pre-written pages | Told you cannot have a lawyer | Threat of arrest for exercising the s.112(2) proviso
Foreigner_Notes: Federal Constitution Art 5(3)-(4) rights (grounds, counsel, 24-hour production) apply to 'a person', not only citizens | Art 5(4) proviso: a non-citizen arrested or detained under immigration law must be produced within 14 days, not 24 hours | Art 5(5): clauses (3) and (4) do not apply to an enemy alien | Consular notification (Vienna Convention on Consular Relations Art 36) is not found in any statute reviewed - Requires Independent Verification | Carry passport/visa or a copy; Immigration Act 1959/63 not reviewed - Requires Independent Verification
Escalation_Path: Lodge a police report at any station (CPC s.107) describing the conduct and officer identity | Complain in writing to the Officer in Charge of Police District (OCPD) / State Police Contingent HQ | Complain to Independent Police Conduct Commission (IPCC) - IPCC Act 2022 not among statutes reviewed; Requires Independent Verification | Contact Bar Council Legal Aid Centre (Red Book front page lists LAC numbers) | SUHAKAM complaint (Human Rights Commission of Malaysia Act 1999 not reviewed; Requires Independent Verification) | Unlawful detention: habeas corpus application to High Court, Federal Constitution Art 5(2) | Civil action for wrongful arrest / false imprisonment / trespass; criminal complaint under Penal Code ss.330, 341-342, 348 where applicable
Research_Notes: Red Book 3.3 says you have the right to ask a lawyer to accompany you; CPC s.112 is silent on counsel for witnesses - treat as Practical Advice / Requires Case Law Review. s.113 limits use of s.112 statements in evidence.

Law: Criminal Procedure Code; Police Act 1967; Road Transport Act 1987
Exact_Citation: CPC s.24(1): person who in presence of a police officer commits or is accused of committing a non-seizable offence and refuses on demand to give his name and residence, or gives a name or residence which the officer has reason to believe to be false, may be arrested in order that his name or residence may be ascertained.
Source_Document: Criminal Procedure Code Act 593 (as at 1 Oct 2022) | Police Act 1967 Act 344 (as at 10 May 2024) | Road Transport Act 1987 Act 333 (as at 1 Apr 2019) | Malaysian Bar Red Book: The Police and Your Basic Rights (May 2023)
Authority_Type: Statute; Bar Council Guidance; Requires Independent Verification (National Registration Act/Regulations not reviewed)
Police_Power: No general statutory duty in the Acts reviewed to identify oneself on demand in all circumstances. Specific triggers: non-seizable offence in officer's presence (CPC s.24); licence/permit stop (PA s.24); roadblock (PA s.26(2)); traffic direction (PA s.21(3)); driving licence/insurance on road (RTA s.58); passengers (RTA s.112(2)).
Required_Legal_Trigger: Offence committed or accused in officer's presence, OR a licence/vehicle/roadblock/traffic context, OR arrest. Otherwise the request is consensual.
Threshold_Type: Offence in presence (s.24) / reasonable grounds (PA s.24(1)(a)(ii)) / none for consensual request
Acceptable_Reasons: Minor offence observed (e.g. littering, traffic) and identity needed for summons | Roadblock | Licence check | Arrest processing
Examples_Of_Legitimate_Reasons: Driver stopped at roadblock asked for licence and IC | Person observed committing a non-seizable offence refuses to give name | Person arrested and being booked
Examples_Of_Insufficient_Reasons: Random demand for IC with no offence, stop or search power cited | Demand to hand over and keep the IC | Demand based on race/appearance alone
Police_Boundaries: May arrest under s.24 ONLY where a non-seizable offence was committed/accused in presence AND name/residence refused or believed false; must release on bond once identity ascertained or produce before Magistrate within 24h (s.24(1))
Police_May_Not_Do: Confiscate the identity card without lawful basis (FC Art 13(1); National Registration law not reviewed) | Detain to 'verify' identity where no s.24 trigger exists | Arrest for refusing to answer questions beyond name/address
Citizen_Questions: Under which power are you asking for my identification? | Am I suspected of an offence? Which one? | Am I under arrest? | Will you return my IC immediately after inspection?
Verification_Steps: Ask officer's name, rank and service number; note them | Plain-clothes: ask for authority card (certificate of appointment, Police Act s.14); Red Book 1.1-1.2: red card = suspended officer, no authority | Uniformed: read name tag and number (Red Book 1.3); note vehicle plate (Red Book 1.4) | Give name, NRIC number and address (Red Book 2.1) - low-cost compliance limits s.24 exposure | Do not hand over wallet; show the card
How_To_Verify_Legality: Check whether any of the trigger contexts exists (offence in presence, licence stop, roadblock, traffic, arrest). If none, the request is consensual; providing name/NRIC/address remains the prudent course (Red Book 2.1).
Required_Documents: None from police for a request; authority card on demand if plain-clothes
Need_Reasonable_Suspicion: Depends on power invoked (see Section column)
Valid_Warrant_Requirements: Not applicable - no warrant involved in this scenario
Indicators_Of_Invalid_Warrant: Not applicable - no warrant involved in this scenario
Can_Refuse: Legally risky - refusal in a s.24/PA s.24/s.26/RTA s.58 context can lead to arrest without warrant; outside those contexts no offence identified in the statutes reviewed, but Requires Independent Verification (National Registration Regulations 1990 reg. on production of IC not reviewed)
Can_Leave: Yes if no stop power or arrest; No while detained under PA s.24(1) for production of licence/permit
Evidence_To_Preserve: Officer name, rank, service number, authority card colour | Date, time, exact location; patrol vehicle plate | Names and contact details of witnesses | Written contemporaneous notes (Red Book 3.3 'Personal Notes') | Any photos/video lawfully taken by bystanders; medical report if injured | Copies of any document handed over (order, warrant, seizure list, receipt)
Red_Flags: IC retained after inspection | Threat of arrest where no offence is alleged | Officer refuses to state the power relied on
Foreigner_Notes: Federal Constitution Art 5(3)-(4) rights (grounds, counsel, 24-hour production) apply to 'a person', not only citizens | Art 5(4) proviso: a non-citizen arrested or detained under immigration law must be produced within 14 days, not 24 hours | Art 5(5): clauses (3) and (4) do not apply to an enemy alien | Consular notification (Vienna Convention on Consular Relations Art 36) is not found in any statute reviewed - Requires Independent Verification | Carry passport/visa or a copy; Immigration Act 1959/63 not reviewed - Requires Independent Verification
Escalation_Path: Lodge a police report at any station (CPC s.107) describing the conduct and officer identity | Complain in writing to the Officer in Charge of Police District (OCPD) / State Police Contingent HQ | Complain to Independent Police Conduct Commission (IPCC) - IPCC Act 2022 not among statutes reviewed; Requires Independent Verification | Contact Bar Council Legal Aid Centre (Red Book front page lists LAC numbers) | SUHAKAM complaint (Human Rights Commission of Malaysia Act 1999 not reviewed; Requires Independent Verification) | Unlawful detention: habeas corpus application to High Court, Federal Constitution Art 5(2) | Civil action for wrongful arrest / false imprisonment / trespass; criminal complaint under Penal Code ss.330, 341-342, 348 where applicable
Research_Notes: National Registration Act 1959 and Regulations 1990 (duty to produce identity card to authorised officers) were NOT among the sources supplied - Requires Independent Verification. Red Book 2.1 'only give your name, NRIC number and address' is guidance.

Scenario: 4. Police demands IC (MyKad) be handed over / retained
Exact_Citation: CPC s.20: on arrest the officer 'may search such person and place in safe custody all articles other than necessary wearing apparel found upon him'. FC Art 13(1): 'No person shall be deprived of property save in accordance with law.'
Source_Document: Federal Constitution (Reprint as at 30 Nov 2025) | Criminal Procedure Code Act 593 (as at 1 Oct 2022) | Malaysian Bar Red Book: The Police and Your Basic Rights (May 2023)
Authority_Type: Constitution; Statute; Bar Council Guidance; Requires Independent Verification
Police_Power: Inspection of the card can be requested (see scenario 3). Taking and keeping the card is a seizure: lawful on arrest (CPC s.20) with safe custody and return on release (Red Book 5.3), or as evidence under a search power with a seizure list (CPC s.64-65).
Required_Legal_Trigger: Arrest (s.20) or lawful search/seizure of the card as evidence. No trigger identified in the statutes reviewed for retaining an IC during a street stop without arrest.
Acceptable_Reasons: Card is itself suspected forged or belongs to another (evidence) | Arrested person's property placed in safe custody
Examples_Of_Legitimate_Reasons: Card suspected to be a forgery is seized and listed | Belongings inventoried at lock-up on arrest
Examples_Of_Insufficient_Reasons: Holding the IC to make the person wait or return later | Keeping the IC as leverage to compel answers | 'Verification' with no arrest and no suspicion the card is false
Police_Boundaries: Seized property must be listed and copy given on request (CPC s.64-65) | Belongings on arrest must be recorded and returned on release (Red Book 5.3; lock-up rules not reviewed)
Police_May_Not_Do: Retain the IC without arrest or seizure basis | Refuse a receipt/list for a seized card | Use the card to coerce cooperation
Citizen_Questions: Are you seizing my IC? Under which section? | Please give me a written list/receipt (CPC s.64-65). | When and where will it be returned?
Verification_Steps: Ask officer's name, rank and service number; note them | Plain-clothes: ask for authority card (certificate of appointment, Police Act s.14); Red Book 1.1-1.2: red card = suspended officer, no authority | Uniformed: read name tag and number (Red Book 1.3); note vehicle plate (Red Book 1.4) | Ask for the seizure list before parting with the card | Photograph the card and the receipt if permitted
How_To_Verify_Legality: Lawful retention is tied to arrest or seizure as evidence with a written list. Mere inspection does not justify retention.
Required_Documents: Seizure list signed by the searching officer (CPC s.64); copy on request (s.65)
Need_Arrest: Yes for s.20 custody of belongings; No for evidence seizure during a lawful search
Valid_Warrant_Requirements: Not applicable - no warrant involved in this scenario
Indicators_Of_Invalid_Warrant: Not applicable - no warrant involved in this scenario
Can_Refuse: May object and request the basis; physically resisting a lawful seizure risks Penal Code s.186/s.353
Evidence_To_Preserve: Officer name, rank, service number, authority card colour | Date, time, exact location; patrol vehicle plate | Names and contact details of witnesses | Written contemporaneous notes (Red Book 3.3 'Personal Notes') | Any photos/video lawfully taken by bystanders; medical report if injured | Copies of any document handed over (order, warrant, seizure list, receipt) | Receipt/seizure list | Time card taken and returned
Red_Flags: No receipt | Card kept while person released | Card handed back only after 'settlement'
Foreigner_Notes: Federal Constitution Art 5(3)-(4) rights (grounds, counsel, 24-hour production) apply to 'a person', not only citizens | Art 5(4) proviso: a non-citizen arrested or detained under immigration law must be produced within 14 days, not 24 hours | Art 5(5): clauses (3) and (4) do not apply to an enemy alien | Consular notification (Vienna Convention on Consular Relations Art 36) is not found in any statute reviewed - Requires Independent Verification | Carry passport/visa or a copy; Immigration Act 1959/63 not reviewed - Requires Independent Verification
Escalation_Path: Lodge a police report at any station (CPC s.107) describing the conduct and officer identity | Complain in writing to the Officer in Charge of Police District (OCPD) / State Police Contingent HQ | Complain to Independent Police Conduct Commission (IPCC) - IPCC Act 2022 not among statutes reviewed; Requires Independent Verification | Contact Bar Council Legal Aid Centre (Red Book front page lists LAC numbers) | SUHAKAM complaint (Human Rights Commission of Malaysia Act 1999 not reviewed; Requires Independent Verification) | Unlawful detention: habeas corpus application to High Court, Federal Constitution Art 5(2) | Civil action for wrongful arrest / false imprisonment / trespass; criminal complaint under Penal Code ss.330, 341-342, 348 where applicable
Research_Notes: No provision in the reviewed Acts authorises retention of an identity card during a non-arrest street stop. National Registration Regulations 1990 not reviewed - Requires Independent Verification.

Scenario: 5. Police requests witness details / asks you to be a witness
Red_Book_Topic: 2.4 When you cannot be arrested; 3. Questioning by the police without arrest
Exact_Citation: CPC s.111(1): officer 'may by order in writing require the attendance before himself of any person who ... appears to be acquainted with the circumstances of the case'. s.111(2): on refusal, officer may report to a Magistrate who may issue a warrant.
Source_Document: Criminal Procedure Code Act 593 (as at 1 Oct 2022) | Penal Code Act 574 (as at 4 Jul 2023) | Malaysian Bar Red Book: The Police and Your Basic Rights (May 2023)
Police_Power: May take witness particulars; may compel attendance by written order (s.111); may require a bond to appear in court (s.118). Every person aware of an offence is bound to inform police (s.13(1)).
Required_Legal_Trigger: Police investigation in progress; person appears acquainted with the circumstances
Acceptable_Reasons: Person saw the incident | Person is complainant | Person has documents relevant to the case
Examples_Of_Legitimate_Reasons: Officer takes names of bystanders after a collision | Written s.111 order served on shop owner holding CCTV
Examples_Of_Insufficient_Reasons: Arresting a witness to make them talk (Red Book 2.4) | Demanding attendance 'now' with no written order and threatening arrest
Police_Boundaries: Compulsion of a witness is by written order then Magistrate's warrant (s.111) - not arrest | Must caution under s.112(4)
Police_May_Not_Do: Arrest a person merely because they are a potential witness (Red Book 2.4; no such power in CPC s.23) | Detain a witness at the station against their will
Citizen_Questions: Am I a witness or a suspect? | Is there a written order under section 111? May I have a copy? | Which report number is this for? | May I attend at a convenient time?
Verification_Steps: Ask officer's name, rank and service number; note them | Plain-clothes: ask for authority card (certificate of appointment, Police Act s.14); Red Book 1.1-1.2: red card = suspended officer, no authority | Uniformed: read name tag and number (Red Book 1.3); note vehicle plate (Red Book 1.4) | Ask for the written order; check it is signed by the investigating officer and states the case | Note that non-attendance is addressed by a Magistrate's warrant, not on-the-spot arrest
How_To_Verify_Legality: A witness can only be compelled by a signed written order (s.111(1)); refusal leads to a Magistrate's warrant (s.111(2)), not arrest by the officer. Disobeying may be an offence (Red Book 3.4; PC s.176 non-furnishing of information - Requires Case Law Review on application).
Required_Documents: Written order under s.111(1) ('Police Order', Red Book 3.2)
Need_Warrant: No (Magistrate's warrant only after refusal of a written order)
Valid_Warrant_Requirements: Not applicable - no warrant involved in this scenario
Indicators_Of_Invalid_Warrant: Not applicable - no warrant involved in this scenario
Can_Refuse: May decline informal requests and offer a convenient time; a written s.111 order must be obeyed (failure is reported to a Magistrate)
Can_Leave: Yes - a witness who is not arrested is free to leave (Red Book 2.3-2.4)
Evidence_To_Preserve: Officer name, rank, service number, authority card colour | Date, time, exact location; patrol vehicle plate | Names and contact details of witnesses | Written contemporaneous notes (Red Book 3.3 'Personal Notes') | Any photos/video lawfully taken by bystanders; medical report if injured | Copies of any document handed over (order, warrant, seizure list, receipt) | Copy of any s.111 order | Your own notes of questions and answers
Red_Flags: Told 'you are arrested as a witness' | Phone seized from a witness without basis | Pressure to sign a statement you did not make
Foreigner_Notes: Federal Constitution Art 5(3)-(4) rights (grounds, counsel, 24-hour production) apply to 'a person', not only citizens | Art 5(4) proviso: a non-citizen arrested or detained under immigration law must be produced within 14 days, not 24 hours | Art 5(5): clauses (3) and (4) do not apply to an enemy alien | Consular notification (Vienna Convention on Consular Relations Art 36) is not found in any statute reviewed - Requires Independent Verification | Carry passport/visa or a copy; Immigration Act 1959/63 not reviewed - Requires Independent Verification
Escalation_Path: Lodge a police report at any station (CPC s.107) describing the conduct and officer identity | Complain in writing to the Officer in Charge of Police District (OCPD) / State Police Contingent HQ | Complain to Independent Police Conduct Commission (IPCC) - IPCC Act 2022 not among statutes reviewed; Requires Independent Verification | Contact Bar Council Legal Aid Centre (Red Book front page lists LAC numbers) | SUHAKAM complaint (Human Rights Commission of Malaysia Act 1999 not reviewed; Requires Independent Verification) | Unlawful detention: habeas corpus application to High Court, Federal Constitution Art 5(2) | Civil action for wrongful arrest / false imprisonment / trespass; criminal complaint under Penal Code ss.330, 341-342, 348 where applicable
Research_Notes: Red Book 3.4 states disobeying a Police Order is an offence - statute reviewed shows the consequence is a Magistrate's warrant (s.111(2)); criminal liability under PC s.176/s.179 (not reviewed in full) Requires Case Law Review.

Scenario: 6. Suspicious person inquiry (loitering, concealment, no account of self)
Red_Book_Topic: 2. When the police questions you; 4. The police arrests you
Exact_Citation: CPC s.23(1)(g): 'any person found taking precautions to conceal his presence under circumstances which afford reason to believe that he is taking those precautions with a view to committing a seizable offence'; (h): 'any person who has no ostensible means of subsistence or who cannot give a satisfactory account of himself'.
Source_Document: Criminal Procedure Code Act 593 (as at 1 Oct 2022) | Federal Constitution (Reprint as at 30 Nov 2025) | Malaysian Bar Red Book: The Police and Your Basic Rights (May 2023)
Police_Power: Arrest without warrant where the s.23(1) conditions are met: reasonable suspicion of a seizable offence (a); housebreaking implements (b); suspected stolen property (d); concealment with intent (g); no satisfactory account (h); reputed habitual offender (i).
Required_Legal_Trigger: Objective facts bringing the person within a specific s.23(1) paragraph. Suspicion must be 'reasonable' (s.23(1)(a)) or circumstances must 'afford reason to believe' (s.23(1)(g)).
Threshold_Type: Reasonable suspicion / reason to believe (arrest); none for a consensual inquiry
Acceptable_Reasons: Person seen trying door handles of parked cars at night | Person hiding in a compound with housebreaking tools | Person carrying goods matching a theft report
Examples_Of_Legitimate_Reasons: Matching description from a report minutes earlier in the area | Observed concealment plus tools | Found in a closed premises without explanation
Examples_Of_Insufficient_Reasons: Being in a 'rough' area | Appearance, ethnicity, nationality, attire | Walking at night with no other fact | Declining a consensual conversation
Police_Boundaries: If arrested, must inform grounds as soon as may be (s.28A(1), FC Art 5(3)) and produce before Magistrate within 24h (s.28(3)) | s.23(1)(h) requires an opportunity to give an account
Police_May_Not_Do: Detain without arrest to 'check background' | Search a non-arrested person on the street absent CPC s.17/s.116A/DDA/AMLA context | Use s.23(1)(h) as a catch-all without giving the person a chance to explain
Citizen_Questions: Am I under arrest? For what seizable offence? | What facts make you suspect me? | May I explain where I am going and show my IC? | Am I free to leave?
Verification_Steps: Ask officer's name, rank and service number; note them | Plain-clothes: ask for authority card (certificate of appointment, Police Act s.14); Red Book 1.1-1.2: red card = suspended officer, no authority | Uniformed: read name tag and number (Red Book 1.3); note vehicle plate (Red Book 1.4) | Give a brief factual account of yourself (addresses s.23(1)(h)) | Ask officer to state the s.23 paragraph relied on
How_To_Verify_Legality: Ask what offence and what facts. A lawful arrest must rest on a specific s.23(1) paragraph and reasonable grounds; if no offence is named and you are confined, this is wrongful restraint unless another power applies.
Required_Documents: None at the moment of arrest; grounds must be stated (s.28A(1))
Need_Arrest: Arrest is the only coercive power here
Valid_Warrant_Requirements: Not applicable - no warrant involved in this scenario
Indicators_Of_Invalid_Warrant: Not applicable - no warrant involved in this scenario
Can_Refuse: May decline consensual questions; cannot resist a lawful arrest (CPC s.15(2); PC s.353)
Evidence_To_Preserve: Officer name, rank, service number, authority card colour | Date, time, exact location; patrol vehicle plate | Names and contact details of witnesses | Written contemporaneous notes (Red Book 3.3 'Personal Notes') | Any photos/video lawfully taken by bystanders; medical report if injured | Copies of any document handed over (order, warrant, seizure list, receipt)
Red_Flags: No offence named | 'We will find something' | Demand for money to be released | Detention in vehicle without being told of arrest

Scenario: 9. Arrest at home (entry into dwelling to arrest)
Exact_Citation: CPC s.16(2): where ingress cannot be obtained, officer acting under warrant, or where a warrant may issue but cannot be obtained without affording the person an opportunity to escape, may 'enter the place and search in it, and ... break open any outer or inner door or window ... if, after notification of his authority and purpose and demand of admittance duly made, he cannot otherwise obtain admittance.'

Examples_Of_Insufficient_Reasons: Entering to 'look around' without a named person to arrest | Non-seizable offence | Forcible entry without first announcing authority and demanding admittance

Scenario: 11. Arrest of witness (person wanted only for a statement)
Exact_Citation: CPC s.111(2): 'If any such person refuses to attend as so required that police officer may report such refusal to a Magistrate who may thereupon in his discretion issue a warrant to secure the attendance of that person as required by such order.'
Source_Document: Criminal Procedure Code Act 593 (as at 1 Oct 2022) | Malaysian Bar Red Book: The Police and Your Basic Rights (May 2023)
Police_Power: None to arrest a mere witness. Compulsion route: written order (s.111(1)) -> refusal reported -> Magistrate's warrant (s.111(2)). Bond to appear at court (s.118); refusal -> court warrant/summons (s.118(3)).
Required_Legal_Trigger: Arrest requires the person to fall within s.23(1) (i.e. suspected of an offence). Witness status alone is not a ground.
Acceptable_Reasons: None for arrest; attendance may be required by written order
Examples_Of_Legitimate_Reasons: Magistrate's warrant issued after a documented refusal of a s.111 order
Examples_Of_Insufficient_Reasons: 'We need your statement now' | 'You will be arrested if you do not come to the station' (no such power) | Reclassifying a witness as a 'suspect' with no facts

Police_May_Not_Do: Arrest or detain a witness (Red Book 2.4) | Hold a witness in the lock-up 'pending statement'

Red_Book_Topic: 2.3 Under arrest; 4.2 Do not resist an arrest
Exact_Citation: CPC s.19(1): 'The person arrested shall not be subjected to more restraint than is necessary to prevent his escape.'
Source_Document: Criminal Procedure Code Act 593 (as at 1 Oct 2022) | Malaysian Bar Red Book: The Police and Your Basic Rights (May 2023)
Authority_Type: Statute; Bar Council Guidance; Requires Independent Verification (Standing Orders)
Police_Power: Restraint incidental to a lawful arrest, limited to what is necessary to prevent escape (s.19(1)); all means necessary if the person resists (s.15(2)).
Required_Legal_Trigger: A lawful arrest + necessity to prevent escape or overcome resistance
Acceptable_Reasons: Risk of flight | Violent resistance | Transport safety of a person arrested for a violent offence
Examples_Of_Legitimate_Reasons: Person attempted to run | Person assaulted officer | Standard transport restraint for serious offence (verify Standing Orders)
Examples_Of_Insufficient_Reasons: Handcuffing a person who is not arrested | Cuffing a cooperative, compliant person for humiliation | Cuffing a witness
Police_Boundaries: Handcuffs mean you are under arrest (Red Book 2.3) so s.28A rights are triggered | Restraint must be proportionate
Police_May_Not_Do: Handcuff without arrest | Apply painful or prolonged restraint beyond necessity (potential PC ss.323, 330, 352)
Citizen_Questions: Am I under arrest? Why? | I am not resisting - are handcuffs necessary? | Please loosen the cuffs; they are injuring me (note the time)
Verification_Steps: Ask officer's name, rank and service number; note them | Plain-clothes: ask for authority card (certificate of appointment, Police Act s.14); Red Book 1.1-1.2: red card = suspended officer, no authority | Uniformed: read name tag and number (Red Book 1.3); note vehicle plate (Red Book 1.4) | Record the time cuffs applied/removed and any injury | Ask for medical attention if injured
How_To_Verify_Legality: Handcuffs are lawful only incidental to a lawful arrest and only to the extent necessary (s.19(1)). Cuffing without arrest has no statutory basis in the Acts reviewed.
Required_Documents: None; station diary should record restraint and injuries (Lock-up Rules not reviewed)
Valid_Warrant_Requirements: Not applicable - no warrant involved in this scenario
Indicators_Of_Invalid_Warrant: Not applicable - no warrant involved in this scenario

Red_Book_Topic: 5.5 How long may the police detain you?
Law: Federal Constitution; Criminal Procedure Code; SOSMA; AMLA; DDA
Exact_Citation: FC Art 5(4): arrested person 'shall without unreasonable delay, and in any case within twenty-four hours (excluding the time of any necessary journey) be produced before a magistrate and shall not be further detained in custody without the magistrate's authority'. SOSMA s.4(5): Superintendent or above may extend detention to not more than 28 days; s.4(10): has effect notwithstanding Art 5 and CPC s.117.
Source_Document: Federal Constitution (Reprint as at 30 Nov 2025) | Criminal Procedure Code Act 593 (as at 1 Oct 2022) | SOSMA 2012 Act 747 (as at 1 Aug 2015) + Amendment Act A1736 (2024) | AMLATFPUAA 2001 Act 613 (as at 1 Jul 2022) | Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 Act 234 (as at 26 Nov 2025) | Malaysian Bar Red Book: The Police and Your Basic Rights (May 2023)
Police_Power: Detain up to 24h (excluding necessary journey) for investigation; beyond that only with a Magistrate's order (s.117). Exceptions: SOSMA security offences (24h + up to 28 days on police authority); non-citizen immigration detention (14 days, Art 5(4) proviso); customs DDA arrests (s.31B, 15 days by Magistrate).
Required_Legal_Trigger: Arrest; for extension, grounds for believing the accusation is well founded and investigation cannot be completed (s.117(1))
Acceptable_Reasons: Journey time genuinely necessary | Remand order obtained
Examples_Of_Legitimate_Reasons: Arrested 8pm, produced before Magistrate next morning within 24h
Examples_Of_Insufficient_Reasons: 'Investigation not finished' without going to a Magistrate | Re-arresting on a new 'offence' to restart the clock without new facts | Counting a long detour as 'journey'
Police_Boundaries: Must produce before Magistrate within 24h or release (s.28, s.29) | Previous detention periods must be disclosed to the Magistrate (s.117(3))
Police_May_Not_Do: Hold beyond 24h without judicial authority (except SOSMA/immigration regimes) | Release and immediately re-arrest to circumvent s.117 (abuse - Requires Case Law Review)
Citizen_Questions: What time was I arrested? | When will I be produced before the Magistrate? | Is this a SOSMA (security offence) arrest?
Verification_Steps: Compute arrest time + 24h | Family/lawyer: attend the Magistrate's court at the expected time | If exceeded: lawyer files habeas corpus (FC Art 5(2))
How_To_Verify_Legality: Detention beyond 24h without a Magistrate's order is unlawful unless SOSMA s.4 or the immigration proviso applies. Ask which regime is relied on.
Required_Documents: Remand order (s.117) beyond 24h; SOSMA s.4(5) written extension by Superintendent+
Valid_Warrant_Requirements: Not applicable - no warrant involved in this scenario
Indicators_Of_Invalid_Warrant: Not applicable - no warrant involved in this scenario
Can_Refuse: N/A
Can_Leave: Must be released at 24h absent a remand order (s.28(3), s.29)

Scenario: 36. Search of persons during a raid
Law: Criminal Procedure Code; Dangerous Drugs Act; AMLA; MACC Act
Exact_Citation: DDA s.27(2)(d): officer executing a s.27 warrant may 'detain every person found in or on such premises, until such premises have been searched'; s.27(1)(b): arrest any person in whose possession drugs are found. Police_Power: Detain everyone present until the premises search is complete; search persons for concealable items (Inspector+ presence under CPC s.17; same gender under s.116A(3)/AMLA/MACC); arrest those found in possession.
Required_Legal_Trigger: Lawful premises search (warrant under CPC s.56 / DDA s.27(1), or without warrant under DDA s.27(4), CPC s.116/s.116A, AMLA s.31, MACC s.31(3))
Threshold_Type: Reasonable cause to believe (warrant) / reasonable cause + delay-frustration (warrantless)
Acceptable_Reasons: Entertainment outlet raided for drugs (Red Book 7.1) | Premises searched for weapons or organised-crime evidence
Examples_Of_Legitimate_Reasons: DDA s.27 warrant for a club; patrons detained and searched by same-sex officers with Inspector present
Examples_Of_Insufficient_Reasons: Searching everyone in a shopping mall with no identified premises/warrant | Strip-searching patrons on the spot (Sch.4 requires arrest and private room) | Searches by junior officers with no Inspector present (s.17)

Threshold_Type: Reason to believe (Magistrate) / reasonable cause to suspect + delay-frustration (warrantless)
Acceptable_Reasons: Named offence under investigation | Specific evidence or thing believed on the premises | Stolen property reported with informant's declaration (s.62)

Examples_Of_Insufficient_Reasons: 'We just want to look around' | Warrant for a different address/unit | 'Routine check' of homes | Search beyond the rooms specified | No list of seized items

Law: Criminal Procedure Code; Computer Crimes Act; Communications and Multimedia Act (not reviewed)
Section: CPC s.20, s.116, s.116A(1)(a)-(b), s.116B; CCA s.10(1)(a); CMA s.249 (not reviewed)
Exact_Citation: CPC s.116B(1): 'A police officer not below the rank of Inspector conducting a search under this Code shall be given access to computerized data whether stored in a computer or otherwise.' s.116B(3): '"access" includes being provided with the necessary password, encryption code, decryption code, software or hardware and any other means required to enable comprehension of the computerized data.' s.116B(2): information so obtained is admissible notwithstanding any other written law.

Research_Notes: PHONE SEARCH FRAMEWORK - Q1 Seizure clearly authorised? YES in context - on arrest (CPC s.20: articles found on the person; 'reason to believe' instrument/evidence); during a lawful premises search (s.56 warrant / s.116 / s.116A(1)(a)); CCA s.10(1) 'seize and detain any such evidence'; AMLA s.31(1)(d); MACC s.31(1)(a). Police_Power: Stored data accessible from a seized/searched device: arguably within s.116B ('stored in a computer or otherwise') and CCA s.10(1)(c). PARTLY - s.116B gives Inspector+ 'conducting a search under this Code' access to computerised data; CCA s.10(1)(a) warrant holder may 'have access to any program or data held in any computer'. PARTLY - s.116B(3) defines access to include 'being provided with the necessary password'; CCA s.10(1)(b) 'reasonable assistance'; s.116B/CCA are silent on the penalty for the suspect's refusal and on the privilege against self-incrimination. Police_Power: Stop a vehicle (uniformed officer, RTA s.55); stop and detain a driver to require production of driving licence/permit (PA s.24(1)(a)); inspect licence and insurance (RTA s.58); arrest without warrant if licence not produced and identity not satisfied (PA s.24(2); RTA s.112(1)(c)).
Required_Legal_Trigger: Driving on a road = licence required (RTA s.26), so PA s.24(1)(a)(i) is satisfied by the act of driving; officer must be in uniform for RTA s.55 duty to stop
Threshold_Type: Low - driving a vehicle is an act requiring a licence; no suspicion needed for a licence stop
Acceptable_Reasons: Licence/insurance check | Traffic offence observed | Roadblock (see scenario 59) | Vehicle matches a report
Examples_Of_Legitimate_Reasons: Uniformed officer signals stop; asks for licence and insurance (RTA s.58) | Vehicle seen running a red light
Examples_Of_Insufficient_Reasons: Plain-clothes person in an unmarked car demanding you stop without identifying (RTA s.123) | Detention beyond the time needed to inspect documents with no further ground (PA s.24(1)(b) proviso by analogy) | Stop targeting a driver's ethnicity/nationality
Police_Boundaries: Officer in uniform for RTA s.55 | Non-uniformed officer must declare office and produce ID on demand (RTA s.123(1)) | Detention limited to the purpose of producing licence/permit (PA s.24(1)(a)) | Arrest only if licence not produced AND name/address not given or not satisfactory (PA s.24(2); RTA s.112(1)(c) proviso)
Police_May_Not_Do: Arrest a driver who produces a valid licence and gives name/address for a minor RTA offence (RTA s.112(1)(c) proviso) | Search the car without reasonable grounds under PA s.24(1)(b) or another power (see scenario 57) | Keep the licence/IC without basis
Citizen_Questions: May I see your authority card? (Red Book 10.2; RTA s.123 - non-uniformed officer must declare office and produce ID on demand) | What is your name, rank and service number; what is your vehicle number? | Why are you stopping/searching my car? (Red Book 10.2) | Am I being investigated or suspected of an offence? Which one? | Am I under arrest? Am I free to go once you have inspected my licence?
Verification_Steps: Ask officer's name, rank and service number; note them | Plain-clothes: ask for authority card (certificate of appointment, Police Act s.14); Red Book 1.1-1.2: red card = suspended officer, no authority | Uniformed: read name tag and number (Red Book 1.3); note vehicle plate (Red Book 1.4) | Stop safely when signalled by a uniformed officer (RTA s.55; PA s.24(3), s.26(2) make failure to stop an offence) | Produce driving licence and insurance certificate on request (RTA s.58(1)-(2)); give name, NRIC, address (Red Book 10.3) | Ask the officer to state the ground for any search (PA s.24(1)(b) requires reasonable grounds to suspect the vehicle is used in an offence) | Stay with the vehicle and watch the search; do not interfere

Required_Documents: Officer's authority card if not in uniform (RTA s.123); driver's licence and insurance certificate (RTA s.58)
Need_Reasonable_Suspicion: No for licence check; Yes for search or extended detention
Valid_Warrant_Requirements: Not applicable - no warrant involved in this scenario
Indicators_Of_Invalid_Warrant: Not applicable - no warrant involved in this scenario
Can_Refuse: Cannot refuse to stop for a uniformed officer (RTA s.55; PA s.24(3)); may refuse directions of a non-uniformed officer who will not identify (RTA s.123(2)); may decline to answer questions beyond identity (Red Book 10.3)
Can_Leave: After licence/insurance inspection, yes unless a further ground is stated (Red Book 10.3: if not arrested you may leave)
Evidence_To_Preserve: Officer name, rank, service number, authority card colour | Date, time, exact location; patrol vehicle plate | Names and contact details of witnesses | Written contemporaneous notes (Red Book 3.3 'Personal Notes') | Any photos/video lawfully taken by bystanders; medical report if injured | Copies of any document handed over (order, warrant, seizure list, receipt) | Dashcam footage | Time stopped and released

Red_Book_Topic: 10. Can the police search your car?
Law: Police Act 1967; Criminal Procedure Code; Dangerous Drugs Act; AMLA; MACC Act
Section: PA s.24(1)(b), (4); CPC s.116A(1)(e), s.20; DDA s.27(8); AMLA s.31(1)(a); MACC s.31(1)(e); RTA s.59 (road transport officer vehicle inspection)
Exact_Citation: PA s.24(1)(b): any police officer may 'stop and search without warrant any vehicle or vessel which he has reasonable grounds for suspecting is being used in the commission of any offence against any law in force: Provided that such vehicle or vessel shall not, subject to subsection (4), be detained longer than is reasonably necessary to complete such search.' DDA s.27(8): police or customs officer 'may stop and search any conveyance which he has reasonable ground for believing to be used for the carriage of any dangerous drug'.
Source_Document: Police Act 1967 Act 344 (as at 10 May 2024) | Criminal Procedure Code Act 593 (as at 1 Oct 2022) | Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 Act 234 (as at 26 Nov 2025) | AMLATFPUAA 2001 Act 613 (as at 1 Jul 2022) | MACC Act 2009 Act 694 (as at 1 Sep 2019) | Road Transport Act 1987 Act 333 (as at 1 Apr 2019) | Malaysian Bar Red Book: The Police and Your Basic Rights (May 2023)

Required_Legal_Trigger: REQUIRED TRIGGER (any one): roadblock/stop PLUS reasonable grounds to suspect the vehicle is being used in an offence (PA s.24(1)(b)) | Reasonable ground to believe carriage of drugs (DDA s.27(8)) | Active investigation with Inspector+ and delay risk for security/organised crime (CPC s.116A) | Search incident to lawful arrest of occupant (scope - Requires Case Law Review) | NOT: curiosity, 'routine', fishing expedition, or the stop itself
Threshold_Type: Reasonable grounds for suspecting (PA s.24(1)(b)) / reasonable ground for believing (DDA s.27(8))
Acceptable_Reasons: Vehicle matches a suspect/stolen-vehicle description | Active anti-drug operation with specific intelligence | Contraband in plain view | Strong smell of drugs | Driver arrested for an offence connected to the vehicle
Examples_Of_Legitimate_Reasons: Vehicle plate flagged as stolen | Driver arrested for trafficking after drugs seen on the seat | Vehicle seen leaving a raided premises
Examples_Of_Insufficient_Reasons: 'Because I said so' | Refusal to give any reason | 'Routine check' of boot with no suspicion | Driver declined to answer questions | Driver's nationality | Fishing for 'anything illegal'
Police_Boundaries: Reasonable grounds must exist before the search | Detention only as long as reasonably necessary to complete the search (s.24(1)(b) proviso) | Vehicle may be moved to police HQ and detained up to 48h or pending proceedings only if reasonably suspected used in or evidence of an offence (s.24(4)) | Items seized to be listed (CPC s.64 applies to Chapter VI searches; for PA searches ask for a list - Practical Advice)
Police_May_Not_Do: Search without stating a ground | Damage the vehicle beyond what the search requires (PA s.26(3) immunity relates to barriers, not searches) | Detain the vehicle beyond 48h without proceedings (s.24(4)) | Plant or 'find' items out of the driver's sight

(Red Book 10.2; RTA s.123 - non-uniformed officer must declare office and produce ID on demand) | What is your name, rank and service number; what is your vehicle number? | Why are you stopping/searching my car? (Red Book 10.2) | Am I being investigated or suspected of an offence? Which one? | Am I under arrest? Am I free to go once you have inspected my licence? | What are your reasonable grounds for suspecting this vehicle is used in an offence? (PA s.24(1)(b)) | May I watch the search? Please list anything you take

Indicators_Of_Invalid_Warrant: Not applicable - no warrant involved in this scenario

Law: Road Transport Act 1987; Criminal Procedure Code; Police Act 1967
Section: RTA s.112(2); CPC s.17 (by analogy - 'place'), s.116A(1)(c), (3), s.20, s.20A Sch.4; PA s.24(1)(b) (vehicle, not persons)

Red_Book_Topic: 10. Can the police search your car?
Exact_Citation: PA s.26(1): 'any police officer may, if he considers it necessary so to do for the maintenance and preservation of law and order or for the prevention or detection of crime, erect or place or cause to be erected or placed any barriers on or across any public road ... and any police officer may take all reasonable steps to prevent any person from passing or any vehicle from being driven past any such barrier.' s.26(2): failure to stop = offence (12 months / RM2,000) and arrest without warrant unless name and address given. RTA s.78(1): uniformed officer authorised in writing by Inspector+ may erect barriers for enforcement of the RTA.
Source_Document: Police Act 1967 Act 344 (as at 10 May 2024) | Road Transport Act 1987 Act 333 (as at 1 Apr 2019) | Malaysian Bar Red Book: The Police and Your Basic Rights (May 2023)

Required_Legal_Trigger: Officer 'considers it necessary' for law and order or prevention/detection of crime (PA s.26(1)) - a subjective, low threshold for the barrier; a search of any particular vehicle still needs s.24(1)(b) reasonable grounds

Examples_Of_Legitimate_Reasons: Roadblock after an armed robbery nearby stopping all vehicles; licence checks
Examples_Of_Insufficient_Reasons: Searching every boot at a licence roadblock with no individual ground | Demanding phone unlock at a roadblock | Collecting 'fines' in cash on the spot

Police_May_Not_Do: Search vehicles indiscriminately | Detain beyond document inspection without a ground | Demand cash

Law: Dangerous Drugs Act 1952; Criminal Procedure Code
Exact_Citation: DDA s.31(1): 'Any police officer or any officer of customs may arrest without a warrant any person whom he reasonably believes to have committed or to be committing an offence against this Act, and every offence against this Act shall be deemed to be a seizable offence'. s.31(2): arrested person 'may be searched at any convenient place provided that no female shall be searched except by a female.' s.37(d): person found with custody or control of anything containing a dangerous drug 'shall, until the contrary is proved, be deemed to have been in possession of such drug and ... to have known the nature of such drug'.
Source_Document: Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 Act 234 (as at 26 Nov 2025) | Criminal Procedure Code Act 593 (as at 1 Oct 2022) | Malaysian Bar Red Book: The Police and Your Basic Rights (May 2023)
Police_Power: Arrest without warrant on reasonable belief of a DDA offence (s.31(1)); search arrested person (s.31(2)); stop and search conveyances on reasonable ground for believing carriage of drugs (s.27(8)); enter premises with Magistrate's/JP's warrant (s.27(1)) or without warrant by Sub-Inspector+ on delay risk (s.27(4)); seize packages/conveyances (s.31(3)).
Required_Legal_Trigger: Reasonable belief of a DDA offence (arrest/person search); reasonable ground to believe drugs carried (vehicle); reasonable cause to believe drugs on premises + warrant or delay risk (premises)
Threshold_Type: Reasonable belief (higher than suspicion on its wording) - Requires Case Law Review
Acceptable_Reasons: Drugs or paraphernalia in plain view | Smell of drugs | Specific intelligence | Person leaving known drug premises during a raid
Examples_Of_Legitimate_Reasons: Officer sees a packet of crystalline substance on the dashboard; arrests and searches driver | Raid under s.27 warrant
Examples_Of_Insufficient_Reasons: Appearance (tattoos, thin build) | Being in an area known for drugs with no other fact | Nervousness alone | Refusal to answer questions
Police_Boundaries: Search after arrest; female by female (s.31(2)) | Sch.4 applies (CPC s.20A(2)) | Persons on raided premises detained only until search completed (s.27(2)(d)) | Seizure list (CPC s.64) | Caution before statement (DDA s.37B(1)(b))
Police_May_Not_Do: Search a person under DDA without arrest (s.31(2) applies to 'every person so arrested') except customs border searches (s.27(9)) | Plant evidence (presumptions in s.37 make this a grave risk - insist on witnessing the search) | Strip search without Sch.4 compliance
Citizen_Questions: Am I under arrest under the Dangerous Drugs Act? What do you reasonably believe I have done? | I want to witness the entire search of my bag/car/room (CPC s.65; Red Book 7.2) | Same-sex officer (s.31(2)) | I will not answer questions until I have a lawyer (DDA s.37B(2))
Verification_Steps: Ask officer's name, rank and service number; note them | Plain-clothes: ask for authority card (certificate of appointment, Police Act s.14); Red Book 1.1-1.2: red card = suspended officer, no authority | Uniformed: read name tag and number (Red Book 1.3); note vehicle plate (Red Book 1.4) | Watch the search continuously; empty your own pockets (Red Book 7.2) | Note where each item was allegedly found and who found it | Ask for the seizure list before leaving the scene
How_To_Verify_Legality: DDA person searches follow arrest on reasonable belief; vehicle searches need reasonable ground to believe carriage of drugs; premises need a warrant or s.27(4) urgency by Sub-Inspector+.
Required_Documents: Warrant (s.27(1)) or s.27(4) basis; seizure list; chain-of-custody records (chemist report later)
Need_Warrant: Premises: yes unless s.27(4); person/vehicle: no
Need_Judicial_Approval: Premises warrant: Magistrate or Justice of the Peace

Law: Dangerous Drugs Act 1952; Criminal Procedure Code
Exact_Citation: DDA s.27(1): Magistrate or JP, 'upon information and after such inquiry as he thinks necessary, that there is reasonable cause to believe that in or on any premises there is concealed or deposited any dangerous drug ... may ... empower such officer by day or by night (a) to enter such premises and there to search for, and seize and detain ...; (b) ... to arrest any person ... in whose possession any dangerous drug ... is found, or whom the officer reasonably believes to have concealed or deposited such dangerous drug'. s.27(4): Sub-Inspector+ may act without warrant where 'by reason of the delay in obtaining a search warrant, the object of the search is likely to be frustrated'.
Source_Document: Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 Act 234 (as at 26 Nov 2025) | Criminal Procedure Code Act 593 (as at 1 Oct 2022) | Malaysian Bar Red Book: The Police and Your Basic Rights (May 2023)
Police_Power: Enter by day or night, break doors, forcibly enter, remove obstructions, detain everyone present until search completed (s.27(2)); arrest persons found in possession (s.27(1)(b)); warrantless entry by Sub-Inspector+ on delay risk (s.27(4)).
Required_Legal_Trigger: Warrant on reasonable cause to believe drugs/articles on premises (s.27(1)) OR Sub-Inspector+ with reasonable cause + delay-frustration (s.27(4))
Acceptable_Reasons: Intelligence of drug storage/consumption at the premises | Observation of dealing
Examples_Of_Legitimate_Reasons: JP warrant for a flat after surveillance | Sub-Inspector enters a club where drugs are being flushed
Examples_Of_Insufficient_Reasons: Raid on an entire apartment block without identifying units | Entry by officers below Sub-Inspector with no warrant | Mass arrest of all patrons without any possession finding or reasonable belief against each
Police_Boundaries: Detention of persons only until the premises search is completed (s.27(2)(d)) | Person search in Inspector's presence (CPC s.17) and same-sex | Arrest requires possession found or reasonable belief against the individual (s.27(1)(b)) | Seizure list (CPC s.64-65)
Police_May_Not_Do: Hold everyone for hours after the search ends | Urine-test persons who are not arrested (s.31A applies to arrested persons - see scenario 63) | Search beyond the premises named
Citizen_Questions: Is there a warrant for these premises? Which Magistrate/JP? | If no warrant: which officer of Sub-Inspector rank or above is relying on s.27(4) and why could a warrant not be obtained? | Has the premises search finished? If so, am I free to go? (s.27(2)(d)) | Am I arrested? On what finding?

How_To_Verify_Legality: Valid warrant (Magistrate/JP) or articulated s.27(4) urgency by Sub-Inspector+. Detention ends when the search ends unless an individual arrest ground exists.
Required_Documents: s.27(1) warrant; seizure list; arrest grounds per person
Need_Arrest: No for detention during search; Yes for continued detention/urine test

Can_Leave: No until search completed; then yes unless arrested

Section: DDA s.31A(1), (1A), (1AA), (1B), (2); s.37(k); s.15 (self-administration offence - verify)
Exact_Citation: DDA s.31A(1): 'When any person is arrested on a charge of committing an offence against this Act ... as give reasonable grounds for believing that an examination of his person will afford evidence ... it shall be lawful for a medical officer acting at the request of any police officer not below the rank of Sergeant ... to make such an examination ... and to use or cause to be used such force as may be reasonably necessary'. s.31A(1A): 'it shall be lawful for a police officer not below the rank of Sergeant ... to require an arrested person to provide a specimen of his urine ... if it is not practicable for the medical officer ... to obtain the specimen'. s.31A(1B): failure without reasonable excuse = offence (fine up to RM10,000 / 4 years). s.37(k): drug found in urine under s.31A -> presumed consumption until contrary proved.
Source_Document: Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 Act 234 (as at 26 Nov 2025)
Police_Power: After ARREST on a DDA charge, with reasonable grounds that examination will afford evidence: medical examination at request of Sergeant+ with reasonably necessary force; Sergeant+ may require a urine specimen where a medical officer is not practicable; refusal is an offence.
Required_Legal_Trigger: (1) Arrest on a DDA charge; (2) reasonable grounds for believing examination will afford evidence; (3) request by Sergeant+ / officer in charge of station / customs officer
Acceptable_Reasons: Arrested for consumption/possession where recent use is suspected (red eyes, paraphernalia, admission)
Examples_Of_Legitimate_Reasons: Person arrested in a raid with a used pipe in pocket; Sergeant requests urine
Examples_Of_Insufficient_Reasons: Urine demanded from a person not arrested | Request by a Corporal/Constable | 'Everyone in the club gives urine' with no individual arrest and grounds
Police_Boundaries: Arrest first | Sergeant+ | Medical officer route preferred; police-collected only if medical officer impracticable (s.31A(1A)) | Chain of custody; analysis by Government science officer (s.31A(1AA))
Police_May_Not_Do: Test non-arrested persons | Use force beyond what is 'reasonably necessary' for the examination | Rely on a specimen collected by an officer below Sergeant
Citizen_Questions: Am I under arrest under the DDA? For what offence? | Which officer of Sergeant rank or above is requiring this specimen? (s.31A(1A)) | Why is a medical officer not available? (s.31A(1A)) | Please seal and label the specimen in my presence; may I note the exhibit number?

How_To_Verify_Legality: Lawful only after arrest on a DDA charge with reasonable grounds, requested by Sergeant+. A demand on a non-arrested person has no basis under s.31A.
Required_Documents: Arrest record; station diary entry of request; exhibit/chain-of-custody form; chemist report later
Need_Reasonable_Suspicion: Yes (reasonable grounds examination will afford evidence)
Valid_Warrant_Requirements: Not applicable - no warrant involved in this scenario
Indicators_Of_Invalid_Warrant: Not applicable - no warrant involved in this scenario
Can_Refuse: Refusal without reasonable excuse is an offence (s.31A(1B)) once lawfully required; refusal of a demand made without arrest or by an officer below Sergeant is not within s.31A - record and seek advice

Scenario: 64. Drug trafficking investigation (detention, statements, bail, presumptions)
Law: Dangerous Drugs Act 1952; Criminal Procedure Code; Evidence Act
Exact_Citation: DDA s.37B(1)(b): statement after arrest inadmissible 'unless the court is satisfied that a caution was administered to him in the following words or words to the like effect - "It is my duty to warn you that you are not obliged to say anything or to answer any question, but anything you say, whether in answer to a question or not, may be given in evidence"'. s.37B(2): after caution the accused 'shall not be bound to answer any questions relating to such case'. s.41B(1): bail shall not be granted where offence punishable with death or imprisonment over five years. s.37(da): possession of threshold weights (e.g. 15g heroin, 200g cannabis, 50g methamphetamine) -> presumed trafficking until contrary proved.
Source_Document: Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 Act 234 (as at 26 Nov 2025) | Criminal Procedure Code Act 593 (as at 1 Oct 2022) | Evidence Act 1950 Act 56 (as at 1 Nov 2017) | Malaysian Bar Red Book: The Police and Your Basic Rights (May 2023)
Police_Power: Arrest/detain; remand up to 7+7 days (CPC s.117(2)(b) - s.39B carries death/life); record cautioned statements admissible under s.37B (overriding CPC s.113/EA s.25-26 where caution given); agent provocateur evidence admissible (s.40A); no bail for serious DDA offences (s.41B).
Required_Legal_Trigger: Reasonable belief of trafficking (s.31(1)); statutory presumptions on weight (s.37(da))
Acceptable_Reasons: Quantity above s.37(da) threshold | Packaging, scales, cash | Communications evidencing sale
Examples_Of_Legitimate_Reasons: 200g+ cannabis in a bag in accused's custody -> arrest for s.39B; remand application under s.117(2)(b)
Examples_Of_Insufficient_Reasons: Trafficking charge threatened to coerce a confession for a lesser offence | Statement taken without the s.37B caution | Denial of lawyer with no s.28A(8) authorisation
Police_Boundaries: Caution before any post-arrest statement (s.37B(1)(b)) | No inducement/threat/promise (s.37B(1)(a); EA s.24) | s.28A rights apply | Remand caps 7+7 (CPC s.117(2)(b))
Police_May_Not_Do: Record a post-arrest statement without the caution and rely on it | Promise a lesser charge for an admission | Hold beyond remand caps
Citizen_Questions: What is the alleged weight and substance? Has a chemist report been obtained? | I have been cautioned; I choose not to answer until I have a lawyer (s.37B(2); Red Book 9.3 'I will answer in court') | I want my lawyer present and my family informed (CPC s.28A)
Verification_Steps: Note whether the exact s.37B caution was given and when | Lawyer: obtain seizure list, exhibit weights, chain of custody; challenge presumptions | Track remand days against the 7+7 cap

Required_Documents: Caution record; seizure list; chemist report; remand orders
Valid_Warrant_Requirements: See remand order requirements (scenarios 24-26)
Indicators_Of_Invalid_Warrant: See remand order indicators (scenarios 24-26)
Can_Refuse: May remain silent after caution (s.37B(2))
Can_Leave: No (s.41B bail bar for serious offences)

Scenario: 65. Arrest of a foreign national (criminal matter)
Red_Book_Topic: 4. The police arrests you (applies to all persons)
Exact_Citation: FC Art 5(3): 'Where a person is arrested he shall be informed as soon as may be of the grounds of his arrest and shall be allowed to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of his choice.' Art 5(4) second proviso: 'in its application to a person, other than a citizen, who is arrested or detained under the law relating to immigration, this Clause shall be read as if there were substituted for the words "without unreasonable delay, and in any case within twenty-four hours ..." the words "within fourteen days"'. Art 8(1): 'All persons are equal before the law and entitled to the equal protection of the law.'
Source_Document: Federal Constitution (Reprint as at 30 Nov 2025) | Criminal Procedure Code Act 593 (as at 1 Oct 2022) | Malaysian Bar Red Book: The Police and Your Basic Rights (May 2023)
Police_Power: Same arrest powers as for citizens (CPC s.23); same 24-hour rule for criminal arrests. The 14-day rule applies only to arrest/detention 'under the law relating to immigration'.
Required_Legal_Trigger: As scenario 8 (seizable offence + reasonable suspicion) - nationality is not a ground
Acceptable_Reasons: As scenario 8
Examples_Of_Legitimate_Reasons: Foreign national reasonably suspected of theft arrested under s.23(1)(a)
Examples_Of_Insufficient_Reasons: Arrest because the person 'looks foreign' | Treating a criminal arrest as an immigration detention to use the 14-day window | Denying a lawyer because the person is not a citizen
Police_Boundaries: Art 5(3) rights apply to every 'person' | 24h production for criminal arrests (Art 5(4) main clause) | s.28A rights apply | Interpreter needed for grounds to be meaningfully communicated (Practical Advice; statute silent)
Police_May_Not_Do: Apply the 14-day immigration proviso to a Penal Code/other criminal arrest | Withhold grounds or counsel on nationality grounds | Seize passport without a stated basis (see scenario 68)
Citizen_Questions: Why am I under arrest? Is this a criminal offence or an immigration matter? | I want to contact my embassy/consulate and a lawyer | I need an interpreter in [language] | Which police station? When will I see a Magistrate?

How_To_Verify_Legality: Criminal arrests of foreigners follow exactly the citizen rules (grounds, counsel, 24h). Only immigration-law arrests have the 14-day production period.
Required_Documents: Same as scenario 8; passport/visa to prove status
Valid_Warrant_Requirements: Not applicable - no warrant involved in this scenario
Indicators_Of_Invalid_Warrant: Not applicable - no warrant involved in this scenario
Can_Refuse: No - do not resist

Exact_Citation: MACC s.44(1): PP or Commissioner+ 'may, where he has grounds to believe that any person who is the subject of an investigation ... is likely to leave Malaysia, by written notice require such person to surrender his certificate of identity, passport or exit permit, or any other travel document'. s.44(3): non-compliance -> arrest and production before a Magistrate; s.44(4): committal up to 14 days until compliance.

Required_Legal_Trigger: MACC investigation + grounds to believe likely to leave (s.44); arrest (s.20); court order; immigration-law powers (unverified)
